info.title: Tolquane Web
info.summary: Create, run, watch and schedule Tolquane flows in a workspace.

get.description: Is this workspace in a git repository, and how much of it is uncommitted?

post.description: ``git init`` here, with a ``.gitignore`` that leaves the server's own files out.

get.description: One old version of a flow, and how it differs from the file as it is now.
The commits that touched this flow, newest first, and whether it has changed.

post.description: Put a flow, and its sidecar, back as they were. Nothing is committed.

get.description: Every ``.py`` file in the workspace, with when it changed and how it last ran.

post.description: Write a new flow from a template or from a model, and return it parsed.
Read source that is not saved yet: the model, or why it is code-only.
The Python for a model. Pure text: nothing is imported or run.

get.description: One flow: its source, its model or why it is code-only, its graph and layout.

put.description:
Write a flow. A ``modified`` that no longer matches answers 409 with the file.

``commit`` asks for the save to be committed with that message, and the
``auto_commit`` setting asks for every save to be. A commit that was asked for
explicitly is checked before anything is written: a workspace with no repository
answers 400 with the file untouched, rather than saving and quietly not committing.

delete.description: Delete a flow and its sidecar.

put.description: Write the canvas sidecar next to the flow.

post.description: Move a flow and its sidecar.

``tq.check`` in a child process: the counts, or the GraphError as it stands.

The imports are probed first, with the interpreter the run would use, and travel
with the failure as well as with the success: a flow that does not check because
``import pandas`` fails is exactly the one whose Problems panel needs the ``pip
install`` line.
``tq.explain``: one line per node and edge.
``tq.draw``: the Mermaid text for the expanded graph.
What ``tq.optimize`` would cut: its notes and the graph it leaves.
Start a flow in a child process and return the run that was recorded.

get.description: Runs, newest first. The log is left out here; ask for one run, or its log.

post.description: SIGTERM now, SIGKILL after ``cancel_grace``. A run that ended is returned as is.

get.description: What the flow printed, live while it runs and from the store afterwards.
The Chrome trace file, for a run started with ``trace``.
Every attempt to tell somebody about this run, sent or failed, oldest first.

post.description: Add a schedule. The cron expression is checked before anything is stored.
What an expression means, and the next five times it fires.
Fire a schedule now, the way the scheduler would.

Send this schedule's notifications now, and say what each channel answered.

The message is the real one, with ``event`` set to ``test`` and the schedule's
last run in it when it has had one. Delivery is not retried here: somebody is
waiting for the answer, and a webhook that is down should say so in ten seconds
rather than in forty.
Sign in. The session token comes back once; it is stored only as a sha256.
Forget this session. A token that is not a session has nothing to forget.

get.description: Who the caller is and what kind of server this is: the page's first question.

post.description: Make the first administrator, from the login page of a ``--token`` server.
Change your own password. Sessions live on: this is the browser that asked.

get.description: Your API tokens. The tokens themselves are not kept, so they are not here.

post.description: Make an API token for scripts. It never expires and is shown this once.

delete.description: Take one of your API tokens back. Anything using it stops working at once.

get.description: Everybody who can sign in, with when each was last seen.

post.description: Add a user with a password they are asked to change at their first sign-in.

put.description: Change a role, disable an account, or set a password the user must change.

delete.description: Remove a user, and with them every session and token they had.

get.description:
Everything the settings page shows. Keys are reported as set, never echoed.

A member sees the workspace and the run settings; whether a key is set, and the
address the server listens on, are an administrator's business.

put.description:
Change any subset. The three secrets -- ``ai.anthropic_key``, ``ai.openai_key``
and ``notifications.smtp_password`` -- go to the key file, never to the store.

post.description: The builder, as an event stream: its words, its tool calls, the flow it wrote.

get.description:
Is the server up, and what is it working on?

No login: this is what a monitor and a login page both ask. Where the workspace
is on disk is not a stranger's business, so it is left out until someone signs in.
